heading: Clock integration
text:
## Clock integration [IRET.14]

The engine does not read a clock. It is **given** its two ([LTIM.2.8.1]):
a monotonic function returning nanoseconds, and a wall function writing UTC
nanoseconds and answering false while it has no reading, sharing one opaque
context pointer handed back on each call. The engine calls them only at the
sample points [LTIM.2.8.4] names.

That indirection is what makes determinism testable rather than merely
intended. The same engine takes wall time in production and a mock clock
under test, with no code path that differs between them — so a recorded
run replays against the recorded `ClockAdvance` values and reproduces
exactly ([LFST.9.2.1]). An engine that called a system clock directly
could not offer that.

The context pointer means the clock needs no globals, so two engines in
one process may run on entirely independent clocks.

The setters are `ds_rete_set_clock`, which takes the monotonic function and
the context, and `ds_rete_set_wall_clock`, which takes the wall function,
both declared in `runtime/src/libds/rete/engine.h`. Each returns
`ds_result_t` and refuses a NULL function with `DS_ERR_INVAL`.
